summary: Plan household surveys, entitlements and livelihood restoration. Explore this practical five-day course and strengthen your resettlement planning.
lede: Land acquisition and involuntary resettlement planning helps project teams identify displacement impacts and document compensation decisions. This intermediate course is for land officers, social-performance specialists and project managers preparing resettlement plans. It covers household census and asset data, eligibility and replacement-cost calculations, and livelihood restoration, consultation and grievance tracking.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits professionals who handle land access, displacement impacts, compensation decisions or resettlement delivery within project planning and implementation. It is designed for roles that need to maintain a credible link between affected-household evidence, entitlements and project records.
prerequisites: Prior experience in land acquisition, project delivery, social performance, compensation or community engagement is recommended. You should be comfortable reviewing basic project and household records; coding or programming is not required.
